key_insight: The paper proposes reducing the separation between modalities by changing the geometry of their shared embedding space—from a unit sphere to a probability simplex. This constrains every embedding to nonnegative values that sum to one.
problem_solved: Multimodal contrastive models such as CLIP and CLAP can place different modalities in separate regions of their shared embedding space, leaving a persistent modality gap.
method: Replace unit-sphere embeddings with probability-simplex representations.
Use nonnegativity and unit-sum constraints as a structural prior shared across modalities.
Change the embedding geometry while retaining the same intrinsic dimension.
impact: This offers practitioners a geometry-based direction for improving cross-modal alignment. The supplied abstract is truncated, so measured improvements and evaluation details cannot be confirmed.
visual_elements: Before-and-after schematic: separated modality clusters versus the intended closer alignment.
Side-by-side geometry diagram: a unit sphere and a triangular probability simplex.
Constraint icons: nonnegative coordinates and components summing to one.
Pipeline diagram: modality encoders → simplex-constrained embeddings → shared representation space.
paper_title: Closing the Modality Gap via Simplex-Constrained Representations
paper_authors: Shubham Gupta, Siva Reddy, Perouz Taslakian, Valentina Zantedeschi, Cem Subakan
